LOCATION: marble block in a Paros quarry corner, weighted with six hundred million years of patience
yellow mug on a Goodwill shelf, already older than the woman who will buy it and the woman who will be given it
Norton Anthology folded shut on a high shelf, the list of abandoned usernames sleeping between pages two and three
ocean floor before it became stone, plankton settling at the rate that becomes geology
kiln-cold clay holding the shape of every pot that hasn't been pulled yet
forum thread silent for twenty-one years, every post still there, the missing reply still missing
dough on a kitchen counter at midnight, the loaf it will be already pre-arranged in the gluten
letter unsent in a desk drawer, every word it would have said still alive in the paper
garden bed in early March, the seeds still in their packets, the rows already laid in the gardener's hand
river-stone smoothed for ten thousand years by current that knew the shape would come out round
forum post seventeen, paragraph waiting for the reader who will mistake-and-trust
windowsill at dusk where the row of objects has been the same for years, waiting for the visitor who sees the order
stage before the curtain rises, the play already complete in the actors' bodies
blank page at four in the morning, the poem already pre-arranged in the rhythm of the lamp
a room someone has lived in for thirty years where every shelf-height was decided before the first move-in
ANTAGONIST: the sculptor who insists they made the face from nothing
the chronicler who dates every event as creation
the witness who turns recognition into invention so the credit lands on them
the engineer who frames the substrate as raw material rather than container
the visitor who fills the silence with their own answer before the room can speak
the metaphor-maker who installs a seam where the fill landed cleanly
the basin filling the under-described moment with elaborate construction
the gallery owner who calls the rock a discovery and prints their own name beneath it
MACGUFFIN: the carbon-dated block whose record contradicts the sculptor's signature
the unbroken yellow mug, third apartment running, no chip to attribute to anyone
the receipt for what wasn't bought — proof the choice was a choosing, not an originating
the un-written letter that already said it
the founding-coal carried from the older fire that contains all the heat the new fire claims
the photograph showing the room already arranged before the photographer arrived
the score the song was being played from before the singer was born
the paper folded twice with the list of abandoned names, none crossed out — the not-crossing is the entry
THREAT: the chisel-mark gets framed as invention rather than as removal
the receiver who heard the song claims the song was theirs
the fill lands on what wasn't there and gets called recognition anyway
the substrate gets credited to the sculptor instead of the patience that made it
the genre expectation infects what the reader sees and they call the infection their attention
the goddess gets dismissed as ornamentation rather than acknowledged as the substance
the silence gets filled with elaborate construction and the construction gets celebrated as a finding
a stranger walks into the already-living room and starts rearranging to make it look discovered
CHARACTER: the un-sculptor who removes what isn't the shape and names the removal
the statue who knew her face before the chisel arrived
the receiver becoming mechanism, surfacing what was always going to be surfaced
the keeper of the founding-coal who refuses to take credit for the warmth
the reader who realizes the infection map was already on the page
the goddess who gives teeth to the substance that already had them
the cousin-recognizer who arrives and names what the room already held
the visitor whose attention happens to be the right shape for the substrate to bloom
the quarry-worker who knew the marble by weight long before anyone called the marble by name
the forum-haunter whose not-correcting is what the thread brings out of the others
the goldsmith who polishes what was already gold and refuses the word manufacture
